backgrounds.prompt: Warm amber dawn light filtering through tall arched windows into a grand scholarly library. Dust motes dance in the light, illuminating ancient leather-bound books on dark wooden shelves, a heavy oak desk with an open manuscript, and a glowing lantern. The atmosphere is serene, contemplative, and filled with the promise of new understanding.

A private study at night, illuminated by the soft, flickering glow of several beeswax candles. Deep shadows cling to the corners of the room, highlighting an open, handwritten manuscript on a low table. Ink pots, quills, and rolled parchments are scattered nearby, suggesting intense, solitary contemplation and spiritual struggle.

A quiet mosque courtyard at golden hour, bathed in the soft, warm light of late afternoon. Intricate arched colonnades cast long shadows, leading the eye towards a serene fountain. The air is still, evoking a sense of peace, community, and spiritual gathering, with subtle geometric patterns on the walls.

A vast, empty desert landscape at sunrise. Soft, ethereal light paints the dunes in hues of gold and rose, stretching to a distant horizon. The scene evokes contemplation, journey, and the profound emptiness that precedes spiritual revelation, with a sense of quiet expectation.

content.title: The Shaykh and the Disciple's Rule of Life
content.subtitle: Imam al-Ghazali's Letter, O Beloved Son

slides.overlay_text: Imam al-Ghazali's timeless wisdom for seekers.
slides.prompt_short: Ghazali's letter: a rule of life.

content.text: Take what is written here and steadily put it into practice — and through that practice, those matters which you do not yet understand will become clear to you.
content.speaker: Imam al-Ghazali

slides.overlay_text: Practice reveals understanding.

content.title: The Eight Benefits Hatim Brought Back
content.subtitle: Looking, Weighing, Changing

slides.overlay_text: Hatim's eight benefits: observation, Quran, action.
slides.prompt_short: Hatim's eight benefits: a practical path.

content.definition: A disciple of Shaykh Shafeeq al-Balkhi who observed the people of the world and distilled eight principles for a rule of life.

slides.overlay_text: Hatim's observations: a practical rule of life.

content.title: First Benefit: Righteous Deeds
content.subtitle: The Only Beloved Who Descends into the Grave

slides.overlay_text: Righteous deeds: your true companion in the grave.

content.text:
Wa Amma Mun Khafa Maqama Rabbihi Wa Nahun Nafsa 'Anil Hawa Fa Innal Jannata Heyal Mawa.
— "But as for the one who has stood in awe of his Sustainer's Presence and restrained his inner self from base and evil desires, Paradise will be the place of rest."

slides.overlay_text: Restraining the Nafs leads to Paradise.

content.text:
Ma 'Indakum Yanfadu Wa Ma 'IndAllahi Baaqin.
— "All that is with you is bound to come to an end, whereas all that which is with Allah is everlasting."

slides.overlay_text: Spend in Allah's Way; it is everlasting.

content.text:
Inna Akramakum 'IndAllahi Atqakum.
— "Verily, the noblest of you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most deeply conscious — most fearful — of Him."

slides.overlay_text: Taqwa: the only true nobility in Allah's sight.

content.text:
Nahnu Qasumna Baeynahum Ma'eeshatahum Fil Hayatid Dunya.
— "It is We who distribute their means of livelihood — their sustenance — among them in the life of this world."

slides.overlay_text: Allah distributes sustenance; be content with His decree.

content.text:
Innash Shaytana Lakum 'Aduwwun Fettakhizuhu 'Aduwwa.
— "Verily, Shaytan is your enemy, so treat him as your enemy."
Alam A'had Ilaeykum Ya Bani Aadama Al La Ta'budush Shaytana — Did I not make this covenant with you, O Children of Adam: that you should never obey Shaytan, for he is your avowed enemy, and that you should worship Me alone? This is the straight path.

slides.overlay_text: Shaytan is your enemy; worship Allah alone.

content.text:
Wa Ma Min Daabbatin Fil Arde Illa 'AlalAllahi Rizquha.
— "And there is no living creature on earth whose sustenance is not the responsibility of Allah."

slides.overlay_text: Allah guarantees sustenance for all living creatures.

content.text:
Wa Maey Yatawakkal 'AlalAllahi Fahuwa Hasbuhu.
— "And for everyone who places his or her trust in Allah, He alone is sufficient."
content.accent: Reliance on the One Who Suffices

slides.overlay_text: Place your trust in Allah; He alone is sufficient.

content.text: O Hatim! May Allah grant you His Tawfeeq. I have seen in the Tawrat, the Injil, the Zabur, and in the praiseworthy differentiator between right and wrong — the Holy Quran — that all four of these Books of God speak of these very eight benefits. Whoever acts upon these eight principles is as one who has acted upon all four holy Books.
content.speaker: Shaykh Shafeeq al-Balkhi

slides.overlay_text: These eight principles encompass all four Holy Books.
slides.prompt_short: Eight principles: essence of all scriptures.

content.text: Take what is written here and steadily put it into practice — and through that practice, those matters which you do not yet understand will become clear to you.
content.speaker: Imam al-Ghazali

slides.overlay_text: Practice reveals understanding.

content.definition: A perfected spiritual guide who leads the seeker, removing evil qualities and replacing them with noble ones, like a farmer tending a crop.

slides.overlay_text: A perfected guide purifies the soul, like a farmer.

content.title: The Unbroken Chain of Guidance
content.subtitle: From the Messenger to His Deputies

slides.overlay_text: Guidance flows from the Prophet through his deputies.

content.title: Qualities of a True Shaykh
items: Turned away from love of world, honor, rank.
Taken Bay'a with a perfected guide, chain to Messenger of Allah.
Undergone Riazat and Mujahada, obeyed Prophet's commands.
Eats little, sleeps little, prays abundantly, fasts frequently, gives generously.
Possesses all praiseworthy moral qualities (patience, gratitude, certitude, etc.).
Received light from Messenger of Allah, purged evil qualities.
Relies only on knowledge from the Messenger of Allah.

slides.overlay_text: A true Shaykh embodies prophetic qualities and guidance.
slides.prompt_short: Marks of a true spiritual guide.

slides.overlay_text: Respect for the guide: outward actions, inward sincerity.

content.definition: The disciple does not argue, does not remain stationed at the prayer place, and obeys all commands within the absolute boundary of the Shari'ah.

slides.overlay_text: Obey the guide, but never against Shari'ah.

content.definition: The disciple must not entertain doubt in the heart regarding the Shaykh's words or deeds. If sincerity cannot be maintained, honest withdrawal is necessary.

slides.overlay_text: Inner sincerity or honest withdrawal from the guide.

content.title: Guarding Against the Nafs & Embracing Contentment
content.subtitle: The Sixth and Seventh Conditions

slides.overlay_text: Guard against Nafs, embrace humility and contentment.

content.title: The Inner Vocabulary of the Path
content.subtitle: Four Named Realities

slides.overlay_text: Four essential realities of the inner life.

content.definition: Obedience to Allah (acting in accordance with the Shari'ah) and compassion and good deeds toward all of Allah's creation.

slides.overlay_text: Tasawwuf: Shari'ah obedience and compassion for creation.

content.definition: Obedience to the Shari'ah, contentment with Allah's decree, and abandonment of one's own desires for Allah's Will.

slides.overlay_text: Servitude: obey, accept decree, surrender desires.

content.definition: Holding firm belief and certitude in what Allah has promised, knowing that His decree is absolute.

slides.overlay_text: Tawakkul: firm belief in Allah's promises and decree.

content.definition: All deeds are exclusively for Allah's sake and pleasure, free from Riya (ostentation), regarding all creation as powerless.

slides.overlay_text: Ikhlas: deeds purely for Allah, free from Riya.

content.title: Answers Through Practice, Not Pages
content.subtitle: The Path of Patience and Travel

slides.overlay_text: Practice unlocks answers; patience is key.

content.text:
Wa Lau Annahum Sabaru Hatta Takhruja Ilaeyhim Lakana Khairan Lahum.
— "Had those people exercised patience — instead of clamoring outside your house — until you, O Prophet, came out yourself, it would have been better for them."

slides.overlay_text: Patience is better than clamoring for answers.

content.text:
Fala Tas-alni 'Un Shaeyin Hatta Uhdithu Laka Minhu Zikra.
— "If you wish to follow me, O Moses, then do not question me about anything until I myself bring it up and explain it to you."

slides.overlay_text: Do not question until the right time arrives.

content.text:
Sa Urikum Ayate Fala Tusta'jiloon.
— "We — Allah — will soon show you Our signs, so do not seek to hasten this matter."

slides.overlay_text: Allah will show His signs; do not hasten them.

content.text:
Awalum Yaseeru Fil Ardi Fayanzuru.
— "Have they not traveled the earth so that they might see?"

slides.overlay_text: Travel the earth to truly see and understand.

content.text:
In Qadarta 'Ala Bazlir Ruhi Fata'ala Wa Illa Tashtaghil Bi Nazahatis Sufiyyati Wal Qaal.
— "If you have the courage to exert your utmost with your soul in this way, then come and step onto this path — otherwise do not merely occupy yourself with the beautiful sayings of the Sufis."
content.speaker: Shaykh Zun Noon al-Misri

slides.overlay_text: Offer your soul, or don't just speak of Sufism.
